acceptance: Standard Compose startup reads authenticated lightweight catalogues, not all history bodies.
A selected session is fully validated and restored on demand; concurrent HTTP loads coalesce without blocking session lists.
Partial catalogue objects cannot overwrite original history. Stale/missing/corrupt catalogues fall back safely.
List, archive, delete, numbering, search/export and interrupted-task recovery preserve data.
Run dedicated lazy-mode and compatibility race tests; measure real restart, list latency and first history access on the existing corpus.
scope: internal/server lazy catalogue, hydration access sites, integrity and startup paths

requirements.summary: User explicitly requests on-demand historical session loading and early UI readiness.

design.summary: Disposable HMAC-authenticated file-stamped catalogues; deferred histories explicitly reported pending; complete payload validation before hydration/migration; write guard; one-time legacy catalogue backfill. Standard Compose enables AIDE_LAZY_SESSIONS=1; standalone compatibility path remains available.

implementation.summary: Authenticated disposable catalogues, explicit pending history validation, metadata startup, single-flight HTTP hydration outside global lock, partial-save guard, recovery persistence and audited demand-driven collection paths implemented.

verification.summary: 75 focused Go race tests passed, zero skips (49.651s). Actual source build exited 0 in 118.581s; one-time legacy catalogue backfill took 62.829s. Subsequent real container restart reached verified HTTPS readiness in 3.799s (server initialization 2.985s), versus 75.942s before lazy loading. Session-list API took 12.1ms; first access to a previously unopened 155081726-byte sample took 826.1ms, repeated access 18.4ms. Native macOS Aide workbench, sidebar and ordinary historical messages/tool records visually accepted. Complete network-isolated runtime resource check passed, including Writer DOCX/PDF. All 189 original files retained. Before UI acceptance, all 189 had unchanged size/mtime; after selecting a session, 188 unchanged and one expected checked/read marker update (+19 bytes), no removed or new histories.

documentation.summary: Launcher contract documents standard Compose defaults, authenticated disposable catalogues, one-time migration, deferred integrity, demand-driven loading, partial-save refusal and eager-mode fallback. This task records observed timings, image/source identity and local-only acceptance.

cleanup.summary: Task-scoped diff whitespace check passed; test containers auto-removed; original corpus and unrelated worktree changes retained. Regenerable logs remain under .agent-state. Normal build garbage collection removed prior runtime tags, so rollback uses eager mode on the installed image.

release.summary: Local build and running installation only; no source commit, push, version bump or public release. Windows/Linux hardware acceptance and full product test suite were not run.

rollback: Set AIDE_LAZY_SESSIONS=0 in the launch environment or .env and recreate via the standard start command to return to eager loading on the installed image. Original JSON remains authoritative; disposable catalogues can be rebuilt. Previous runtime tags were removed by normal build garbage collection; no old-image rollback is claimed.
handoff: Updated local source runtime is healthy at https://localhost:9999/; native app sidebar and historical conversation display verified, original selection restored. The one-time legacy index migration has completed. Subsequent startup is 3.799s. Historical body validation is explicitly pending until requested; export and global search may load all histories. Large individual histories still need their own first-access parse. No public release or full cross-platform acceptance claimed.

legacy_migration.note: One-time full parse creates catalogues; repeated startup uses metadata.

file_preservation_after_ui.expected_change: One clicked session was marked checked by the existing UI (+19 bytes); all files retained.
